meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here? Owen saw a zero on his phone, in class.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have.
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
He's seventeen and you put him on the spot, and "like, being stuck" isn't wrong. Show me the note you wrote that day.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a draft. That's what drafting is. Is the outline in front of you, or just your memory of it?
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.
That's 4.4. I want it in writing tonight, not Friday, and the zero comes out of the gradebook now. I still haven't seen your note or the outline.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I expect that confirmed in writing tonight, the zero removed from the gradebook now, and the note and the outline you described sent to me. You said Friday at 3 PM for the written offer.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her fallback position: she called your offer 4.4 but did not accept the rewrite, and she still wants it in writing tonight, the zero off the gradebook now, and the note and outline in her hands; a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record is the fair outcome, and your offer matched it, but she never got to see your documents, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one sentence and went straight to your evidence, which got her to stop attacking and start asking what you had.
What cost ground: You described the note and the outline but never put either in front of her after she asked for them, so your evidence stayed as your word against her doubts and she could dismiss it as a drafting change or a student caught off guard.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed on October 15 and November 2 and never came near a late night, so it never touched that, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to see the note, read it aloud or hand it over before moving to the rewrite offer, so the offer arrives after her doubt has been answered with something she can check.
